stem: The same SageMaker Pipeline definition must run in dev with `ml.m5.large` instances and 10% sample data, and in prod with `ml.p3.2xlarge` instances and full data, without maintaining two copies of the pipeline code. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: Keep two Git branches with different hard-coded instance types and data paths and deploy whichever branch matches the account
Store the values in a notebook that edits the pipeline's JSON definition by hand before each run in the target account
Create two separate pipelines with different names and copy every step definition from the dev pipeline into the prod pipeline
Define `ParameterString` values for the instance type and input path and override them in `pipeline.start()` for each environment

stem: Data scientists have tested Python functions for preprocessing, training and evaluation in notebooks. They want to turn them into a SageMaker Pipeline with minimal rewriting, keeping the functions as plain Python. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: Schedule the notebooks with cron on a SageMaker notebook instance so they run one after the other in the required order
Decorate the functions with the `@step` decorator from the SageMaker Python SDK and build the pipeline from the step outputs
Rewrite every function as a separate Docker image and reference each image from its own custom container processing step
Convert the functions into AWS Lambda functions and chain them with Lambda steps, since Lambda runs plain Python code

stem: A large model runs on a real-time endpoint with 16 GPU instances. The team wants guarded updates with automatic rollback on CloudWatch alarms, but the account's GPU quota cannot fit a second full fleet during the update. Which deployment option fits BEST?

choices.text: A rolling deployment that replaces instances in small batches, with alarms that trigger an automatic rollback if they fire
Deleting the endpoint and creating a new one with the updated model, followed by a manual check of the CloudWatch alarms
A blue/green update with all-at-once traffic shifting, because it provisions the new fleet and switches traffic in a single step
A blue/green update with canary traffic shifting that sends 10% of traffic to a full new fleet before the remaining 90% moves

stem: A company wants an internal assistant on Amazon Bedrock that answers employee questions from 40,000 policy documents. About 200 documents change every day, answers must cite the source document, and the team has no labeled question-answer pairs. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: Create an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base over the documents and answer with retrieval-augmented generation that returns citations
Fine-tune a Bedrock foundation model every night on the full document set so that the model memorizes the newest policy wording
Run continued pre-training every week on the changed documents so the model absorbs the new policy text before users ask about it
Paste as many complete policy documents as fit into every prompt so the model can read the relevant text directly for each question

stem: An online bank wants to flag logins where a customer account signs in from an IP address that is unusual for that particular account. It has 18 months of login logs with account IDs and IPv4 addresses but no labeled fraud examples. Which SageMaker built-in algorithm fits BEST?

choices.text: Random Cut Forest, trained on the IPv4 addresses converted to integers to find outlying address values
XGBoost, trained as a binary classifier on the login logs to predict which sign-ins are fraudulent ones
IP Insights, trained on account ID and IP address pairs to score how unusual each new pairing is
K-means, trained on the IPv4 octets to group addresses and flag logins that fall into the small clusters

stem: A manufacturer wants to extract its own part numbers (such as `HX-4471-B`) and internal failure codes from 300,000 free-text technician notes. Amazon Comprehend's standard entity detection does not return these as distinct types. The team has lists of known part numbers and codes but no ML engineers. Which option fits BEST?

choices.text: Amazon Comprehend topic modeling run on the notes so that part numbers and failure codes are grouped together into their own topics
Amazon Comprehend custom entity recognition trained with the existing entity lists for the part numbers and the failure codes
Amazon Textract with Queries that ask for the part number and failure code in each note that has been stored as a plain text file
The Comprehend DetectEntities API with the COMMERCIAL_ITEM entity type selected so that every part number is labeled correctly

stem: A SageMaker hyperparameter tuning job runs a custom PyTorch script. Every training job completes, but the tuning job shows no objective metric values. The metric definition uses the regex `val_loss=([0-9\.]+)`, and the script's log lines look like `epoch 5 validation loss: 0.2310`. What should the engineer do?

choices.text: Enable SageMaker Debugger on the training jobs so that it collects the validation loss tensors and passes them to the tuner
Increase MaxRuntimeInSeconds for each training job so the script has enough time to write its final validation metric line
Change the tuning strategy from Bayesian to random search so that the objective metric does not need to be read from the logs
Fix the metric definition regex, or the script's log format, so the regex matches the validation loss lines the script prints

stem: An image model trained on one GPU with batch size 64 and learning rate 0.01 reaches 91% accuracy. The team moves to SageMaker distributed data parallel on 8 GPUs, keeping 64 images per GPU, the same learning rate and the same 30 epochs. Training is 7 times faster, but accuracy drops to 84%. The team wants to keep the speedup. What should it change FIRST?

choices.text: Scale the learning rate up in proportion to the larger global batch, with a short warm-up period at the start of training
Switch from data parallelism to model parallelism so that each GPU holds a part of the model instead of a full copy
Increase the number of epochs from 30 to 240 so that the model receives as many weight updates as it did on one GPU
Lower the per-GPU batch size to 8 so that the global batch size across all eight GPUs goes back to the original 64

stem: A single-instance SageMaker training job reads 1.5 TB of images from S3 in File mode. Each run spends about 40 minutes copying data before the first epoch starts. The training script opens image files from a local directory, and the team does not want to change how it reads data or build new storage infrastructure. Which change fits BEST?

choices.text: Increase the job's VolumeSizeInGB so that the full dataset copy completes faster on a larger ML storage volume before training
Switch the input channel to Pipe mode so that data is streamed from S3 directly into the training container as it is needed
Switch the input channel to FastFile mode so that S3 objects appear as local files and are streamed on demand while training
Set the channel's S3DataDistributionType to ShardedByS3Key so that the instance downloads only a portion of the objects in S3

stem: A fraud model uses the SageMaker built-in XGBoost algorithm with `objective=binary:logistic`. Only 0.8% of training rows are fraud. With `eval_metric=error` and early stopping, the model predicts almost no fraud, yet validation error is only 0.8%. Which TWO changes are MOST appropriate? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Remove early stopping and set `num_round` to 5,000 so that the trees keep learning until they finally fit the fraud rows
Set `eval_metric` to `aucpr` so that early stopping and model selection track how well fraud cases are ranked
Change the objective to `multi:softmax` with `num_class=2` so that the two classes are learned as separate outputs
Set `subsample` to 0.1 so that each boosting round sees fewer legitimate rows and the classes appear more balanced
Set `scale_pos_weight` to about the ratio of negative to positive rows so that errors on fraud rows weigh more

stem: A tuning job for a gradient boosting model searches 8 continuous hyperparameters with the Bayesian strategy, `MaxNumberOfTrainingJobs=100` and `MaxParallelTrainingJobs=100`. The best result is no better than what random search found earlier. Which change is MOST likely to improve the Bayesian search?

choices.text: Enable warm start from the earlier random search and also raise MaxParallelTrainingJobs to 200 to explore more combinations
Set the scaling type of every hyperparameter to Logarithmic so that the search explores a wider range of values in each run
Switch to the grid search strategy so that every combination of the eight continuous hyperparameters is tried at least once
Lower MaxParallelTrainingJobs to a small number, such as 5, so each new batch of jobs can use the results of completed jobs

stem: A team must adapt a 13-billion-parameter open language model to its support-ticket style on SageMaker. Its budget allows one ml.g5.2xlarge instance with a single 24 GB GPU. Full fine-tuning runs out of GPU memory immediately. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: Full fine-tuning with batch size 1 and gradient checkpointing so that activations are recomputed and the whole model fits in memory
Parameter-efficient fine-tuning with LoRA adapters on a 4-bit quantized copy of the base model (QLoRA) so only small adapters train
Full fine-tuning with a much larger dropout rate so that fewer neurons are active in each step and the memory needed is much lower
Pre-training a new 13-billion-parameter model from scratch on the support tickets so that the whole model learns the company style

stem: Before training a loan-approval model, a compliance team wants to know whether the historical labels already approve applicants aged 60 or over at a lower rate than younger applicants. No model exists yet. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: Run a SageMaker Clarify post-training bias analysis and review Disparate Impact (DI) for predictions made on the age facet
Run a SageMaker Clarify pre-training bias analysis and review the Class Imbalance (CI) metric for the age facet in the data
Run a SageMaker Clarify pre-training bias analysis and review the Difference in Proportions of Labels (DPL) for the age facet
Schedule SageMaker Model Monitor bias drift monitoring on the endpoint and alarm when the age-group metrics begin to differ

stem: Instance metrics show that a PyTorch image training job on an ml.p3.8xlarge instance keeps GPU utilization around 25%. One CPU core is at 100% while the others are mostly idle, and the DataLoader decodes and resizes full-size JPEGs every epoch. Which TWO actions will MOST improve GPU utilization? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Resize and encode the images once in a SageMaker Processing job so the training job reads smaller, ready-to-use inputs every epoch
Split the model across the GPUs with model parallelism so that each GPU runs fewer layers and waits less for every training batch
Move the training job to an ml.p4d.24xlarge instance so that the model has faster GPUs with more memory available for each batch
Increase the learning rate and the number of epochs so that the GPUs perform more useful work each time a new batch reaches them
Increase the DataLoader `num_workers` so that several CPU processes decode and augment images in parallel with the training steps

stem: A team has fine-tuned two candidate models for summarizing support conversations and wants to compare them on 2,000 prompts for correctness, completeness and helpfulness. ROUGE scores do not reflect quality well, and no human reviewers are available. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: An Amazon Bedrock programmatic evaluation job that scores the similarity of each summary to a set of reference summaries
An Amazon Bedrock model evaluation job that uses a human-based workflow with a work team made up of the company's own employees
Amazon CloudWatch metrics for each model's invocation latency and output token count, compared over several days of test traffic
An Amazon Bedrock model evaluation job that uses a judge model (LLM-as-a-judge) to score each response on the chosen metrics

stem: A credit model's SageMaker Clarify SHAP report is confusing: nearly every applicant gets a large positive attribution for `age` and `income`. The analysis configuration uses a baseline record where every feature, including age and income, is set to 0. What should the engineer change?

choices.text: Use a representative baseline, such as a summary of the training data from K-means centroids, instead of the all-zero record
Remove `age` and `income` from the model inputs so that the other features receive a fairer share of every applicant attribution
Replace SHAP with partial dependence plots so that each feature's average effect is shown without having to use any baseline
Increase `num_samples` in the SHAP configuration so the Kernel SHAP estimates become more precise for every applicant record

stem: A model scores 5 million insurance records every night with a SageMaker batch transform job, and no real-time endpoint exists. The team wants automated reports and alerts when the input feature distributions drift from the training baseline. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: Create CloudWatch anomaly detection alarms on the batch transform job's duration and instance CPU utilization for every nightly run
Deploy a real-time endpoint only to enable data capture, send each night's records through it, and attach a Model Monitor schedule
Enable data capture in the batch transform job and create a Model Monitor data quality schedule that reads the captured batch data
Run a SageMaker Clarify explainability job every night on the scored output and compare the global SHAP values with the last run

stem: A day after a new mobile app release, the `Invocation4XXErrors` metric of a SageMaker real-time endpoint jumps, while `Invocation5XXErrors`, `ModelLatency` and CPU utilization stay unchanged. The model and endpoint were not modified. What should the team do FIRST?

choices.text: Raise the container's model server timeout and worker count so that long-running requests from the new app have more time to finish
Increase the endpoint's instance count and lower the auto scaling target value so that more capacity absorbs the new mobile traffic
Roll the endpoint back to the previous model version because the new release has exposed a defect inside the model artifact itself
Compare the new app's request payloads and ContentType with what the container expects, using the endpoint logs for rejected calls

stem: A Model Monitor data quality schedule runs hourly on an endpoint with 60 features. The team wants a CloudWatch alarm only when the drift distance of two critical features, `credit_utilization` and `income`, exceeds a threshold, not for every violation in the report. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: Create an EventBridge rule on the monitoring job's completion event and send every completed execution to an SNS topic for review
Enable CloudWatch metrics publishing in the monitoring schedule and alarm on the drift metrics for those two features only
Configure a CloudWatch Logs metric filter that counts every violation line in the monitoring job logs and alarm when it exceeds 1
Enable an alarm on the endpoint's Invocations metric so the team is notified whenever the request volume changes significantly

stem: Several internal applications call foundation models through the Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel and Converse APIs. Compliance now requires keeping the full prompt and response text of every call for one year, searchable for investigations. Which solution fits BEST?

choices.text: Create CloudWatch dashboards for the Bedrock Invocations, InputTokenCount and OutputTokenCount metrics with one year of retention
Enable Amazon Bedrock model invocation logging with delivery to Amazon S3 and CloudWatch Logs, and set the retention periods to one year
Create an AWS CloudTrail trail for all Regions that stores Bedrock API events in S3, and query the stored events with Amazon Athena
Attach an Amazon Bedrock guardrail to every application's calls so that each prompt and response is filtered and stored before return

stem: An endpoint captures 100% of requests and responses, about 2 TB per day in S3, for hourly data quality and daily model quality monitoring. Captured data is never used after 30 days, and storage cost is rising fast. Which TWO changes reduce cost while keeping both kinds of monitoring? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Add an S3 Lifecycle rule that expires captured objects older than 30 days under the endpoint's data capture prefix in the bucket
Change the data capture options to capture only the request input so that the stored response data is no longer kept in the bucket
Suspend the monitoring schedules on weekends so that the monitoring jobs do not read captured data on Saturdays and Sundays
Add an S3 Lifecycle rule that moves captured objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive as soon as they are written to the capture prefix
Lower the data capture sampling percentage to a level, such as 10%, that still gives each monitoring run a representative sample

stem: A SaaS company has 900 small XGBoost models, one per tenant, each on its own ml.m5.large real-time endpoint that is under 3% utilized. All models use the same container. The company wants to cut hosting cost and the number of endpoints to manage, and an occasional slower first request for a rarely used tenant is acceptable. Which option fits BEST?

choices.text: Keep one endpoint per tenant but switch every endpoint to an ml.t2.medium instance so that each tenant's endpoint costs much less
Combine the 900 models into one multi-container endpoint so that each tenant model runs in its own container behind one endpoint
Host all tenant models on a small number of SageMaker multi-model endpoints that load each model from S3 when a request needs it
Move every tenant model to its own serverless inference endpoint so that each tenant is billed only for the requests that it sends

stem: Data scientists use SageMaker Studio JupyterLab spaces on ml.g5.xlarge instances. Cost reports show many of these apps running all night and through weekends with no activity. Administrators want an automatic control that does not depend on users remembering to stop apps. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: Send a daily email reminder with Amazon SNS each evening that asks every user to stop the running JupyterLab applications
Buy a SageMaker Savings Plan that covers the ml.g5.xlarge usage so that the hours spent idle are billed at a lower rate
Reduce the default EBS volume size of each JupyterLab space so that the storage attached to the idle apps costs much less
Configure idle shutdown for JupyterLab apps in the SageMaker domain settings with an idle timeout such as 60 minutes

stem: Each data science team has its own sandbox AWS account in AWS Organizations. When a sandbox account's actual monthly spend passes its budget, finance wants new SageMaker training jobs and endpoints in that account blocked automatically until an administrator reviews it. Which solution fits BEST?

choices.text: Cost Explorer forecasts reviewed every week by the finance team, who then manually delete SageMaker resources in any overspending account
An AWS Budgets budget per account with a budget action that applies an SCP denying SageMaker create actions when the budget is exceeded
Service Quotas requests that lower each sandbox account's SageMaker instance quotas so that the accounts cannot run many instances
AWS Cost Anomaly Detection monitors for each sandbox account that send alerts to the finance team whenever unusual spend patterns appear

stem: A training data bucket has a policy that denies all S3 access unless `aws:SourceVpce` equals the VPC's S3 gateway endpoint. Studio notebooks in the VPC read the data fine, but SageMaker training jobs now fail with AccessDenied even though their execution role allows `s3:GetObject`. The jobs are created without a VpcConfig. What should the engineer do?

choices.text: Add `s3:ListBucket` and `s3:GetObject` for the bucket to the execution role again so that the role permissions are refreshed

Run the training jobs with a VpcConfig that uses subnets whose route tables include the S3 gateway endpoint for the data bucket
Enable network isolation on the training jobs so that SageMaker downloads the training data only over the private AWS network

choices.text: Add an `aws:SourceIp` condition for 198.51.100.0/24 to the IAM policy that allows `sagemaker:CreatePresignedDomainUrl` for users

Lower SessionExpirationDurationInSeconds for the presigned domain URLs so that each user's Studio session must be renewed more often
Set the domain's network access type to VpcOnly so that all Studio app traffic flows through the bank's own VPC, subnets and endpoints

Jobs that do not comply must be rejected at creation. Which TWO IAM policy conditions should deny `sagemaker:CreateTrainingJob`? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Deny when the `aws:SecureTransport` condition key is false, so that the job and all of its data stay inside of the company VPC

choices.text: Store the password in a String parameter of Systems Manager Parameter Store and pass only the parameter name to the processing job
Build the password into the processing container image and store that image in a private Amazon ECR repository with scanning on
Pass the password as a container argument instead of an environment variable so that it no longer appears in the job settings
Store the password in AWS Secrets Manager, pass only the secret name, and let the job's execution role read the secret at runtime

stem: A data scientist has `sagemaker:CreateTrainingJob` permission and calls it with `RoleArn` set to the team's existing SageMaker execution role. The call fails with "User is not authorized to perform iam:PassRole on resource" and names that role. The execution role itself already has all the S3 and ECR access the job needs. Which change fixes the error while keeping least privilege?

choices.text: Add the data scientist's IAM user to the trust policy of the execution role so that the user can assume the role directly
Attach the AmazonS3FullAccess managed policy to the data scientist so that SageMaker can read the training data on the user's behalf
Allow iam:PassRole on the ARN of that one execution role, with the iam:PassedToService condition set to sagemaker.amazonaws.com
Attach the AdministratorAccess managed policy to the data scientist so that any role in the account can be handed to SageMaker jobs

stem: Applications in a private VPC call a SageMaker real-time endpoint through an interface VPC endpoint for the SageMaker Runtime service. The security team wants to make sure those applications can invoke only the `fraud-scoring` endpoint and cannot use the same network path to invoke any other endpoint, including endpoints in other AWS accounts. What should the ML engineer do?

choices.text: Attach a VPC endpoint policy that allows sagemaker:InvokeEndpoint only on the fraud-scoring endpoint ARN and denies it for other resources

stem: A partner company in a different AWS account must send real-time inference requests to a SageMaker endpoint in the model-owner account. The model-owner's security team wants no long-term IAM access keys shared with the partner and wants permission limited to invoking that one endpoint. Which TWO steps meet these requirements? (Select TWO)

choices.text: In the model-owner account, add a resource-based policy to the SageMaker endpoint that names the partner account as the allowed principal
In the model-owner account, create an IAM role that trusts the partner account and allows only sagemaker:InvokeEndpoint on that endpoint ARN
In the partner account, copy the model artifacts to a local bucket and deploy a second endpoint that the partner's applications call directly

In the partner account, allow the calling application's role to call sts:AssumeRole on the model-owner role and use the temporary credentials

stem: Data scientists clone a private GitHub repository into SageMaker Studio. A security review found the personal access token pasted into notebook cells and shared in chat. The team wants Studio to authenticate to the repository without any person handling the token. What should the ML engineer do?

Store the token in an S3 object with a public read block and have every notebook download the object at startup to configure git

stem: A team trains a model in one account with output encrypted by a customer managed KMS key using SSE-KMS. In the deployment account, creating a SageMaker endpoint fails with an AccessDenied error while the container downloads model.tar.gz. The deployment execution role has `s3:GetObject` on the artifact bucket, and the bucket policy allows that role. What is the most likely missing piece?

The endpoint configuration must set network isolation so that the artifacts are decrypted before the container starts downloading

stem: Three teams share one SageMaker Studio domain. The fraud team's data lives in a bucket that the marketing team must never read, and the reverse also applies. Today every user profile inherits the domain's default execution role, which can read both buckets. The company wants to fix this without creating a separate domain for each team. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: Create one execution role per team with access to only that team's bucket and assign it to each team's user profiles or spaces

Keep the default execution role and ask each team to avoid opening the other team's bucket in their notebooks and jobs
Move all of the data into a single shared bucket and separate the teams with different folder names that they agree to use

stem: An auditor asks a bank which employees and roles read the customer files in the training data bucket during the last quarter. The bank has a CloudTrail trail that records management events for all Regions, but the auditor finds no `GetObject` entries. What should the ML engineer do to answer this kind of question going forward?

choices.text: Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights on the SageMaker training log group to find the users who read the bucket objects

Turn on AWS Config recording for the bucket so that a configuration item is stored each time a training job reads an object

stem: A training job runs with `EnableNetworkIsolation` set to true because the data is sensitive. The training script runs `pip install` for two libraries and calls boto3 to read a reference dataset from a second S3 bucket. The job fails inside the script with connection errors, but the main input channel is read correctly. Which change fixes the failure while keeping the isolation?

choices.text: Attach an S3 gateway endpoint policy that allows the second bucket so that the isolated container can call the S3 API directly

Build the libraries into the training image and supply the reference dataset as an additional S3 input channel of the training job
Grant the training execution role s3:GetObject on the second bucket so that the calls made from the script are authorized

stem: A company exposes a chat assistant built on an Amazon Bedrock foundation model. Compliance requires that email addresses and phone numbers a user types are not sent to the model in raw form and that any such data in a reply is masked, without changing the application's prompt logic. Amazon Bedrock Guardrails with a sensitive information filter configured to mask personal data types in inputs and in model responses

stem: A platform team must guarantee that no SageMaker notebook instance in the company account can be created with root access enabled, whatever permissions a user's own IAM policy grants. Which approach enforces this?

stem: An application in a private subnet calls a SageMaker real-time endpoint through an interface VPC endpoint for `sagemaker.runtime`. stem: A training job is configured with private subnets and no NAT gateway or internet gateway. The subnets already have a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. stem: A team runs a SageMaker Model Quality monitoring schedule for a churn endpoint. Ground truth files are uploaded to Amazon S3 each week. The monitoring executions complete, yet the reports contain no accuracy or AUC values and a note says no records could be merged with ground truth. Which TWO actions are needed to fix this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Replace the Model Quality schedule with a Data Quality schedule because ground truth is only used by data quality monitoring

stem: A lending model's feature attribution drift monitor, configured with SageMaker Clarify, reports a violation even though all input feature distributions still match the data quality baseline. Which statement explains what the monitor compares and why this can happen?

It compares the mean and standard deviation of each input column in live data with the training statistics, using a Kolmogorov-Smirnov test

stem: A retailer scores 2 million customers every night with a SageMaker batch transform job, and no real-time endpoint exists. The ML team wants to know each morning whether the input feature distributions differ from the training data, using SageMaker's managed monitoring tools. What should the ML engineer do?

choices.text: Enable data capture on the transform job, then create a Model Monitor schedule that uses the captured batch input as its source and checks it against a baseline
Deploy a real-time endpoint next to the batch job and mirror a sample of nightly records to it so that endpoint data capture works
Write a scheduled AWS Glue job that computes column statistics of the nightly file and publishes the values as a custom CloudWatch metric
Turn on SageMaker Debugger on the batch transform job so that it profiles the feature distribution of every nightly input file

stem: An application calls Amazon Bedrock models on demand. During peak hours some calls fail because the account exceeds its quota, and the on-call team learns about it only from user complaints. The team wants an automatic notification as soon as Bedrock throttles requests, with the least effort. What should the ML engineer do?

choices.text: Turn on model invocation logging to S3 and run an hourly Athena query that counts records that report a throttling error, then emails the result
Create an AWS Config rule that marks the account non-compliant whenever the application receives more throttled Bedrock requests than the quota
Create a CloudWatch alarm on the InvocationThrottles metric in the AWS/Bedrock namespace and send the alarm state changes to an Amazon SNS topic
Create a CloudTrail trail for management events and set an alarm on the Bedrock InvokeModel event, which reports each quota failure separately

stem: A team hosts a real-time endpoint that receives large request payloads. For drift monitoring they only need about one in ten requests, and they only need the request features, not the model's responses, in the capture files. Which endpoint configuration meets this with the lowest storage volume?

choices.text: Enable data capture with InitialSamplingPercentage set to 10 and a CaptureOptions list that contains only the Input capture mode
Enable CloudWatch Logs for the endpoint container and filter every tenth request line into a log group for monitoring to read
Enable data capture with InitialSamplingPercentage set to 100 and delete the response files from the S3 capture location every night
Enable data capture with InitialSamplingPercentage set to 10 and CaptureOptions that list both the Input and Output capture modes

stem: A demand-forecast endpoint has a Model Monitor data quality schedule and a model quality schedule, each emitting CloudWatch metrics. Retraining costs about $3,000 per run, and the drift alarm on one feature fires several times a month even though forecast accuracy stays within target. The team wants to retrain only when there is evidence of harm. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: Lower the data quality constraint thresholds so that the drift alarm fires more often and retraining happens earlier
Create a composite alarm that is in ALARM only when the feature drift alarm and the model quality alarm are both in ALARM
Disable the model quality schedule and use only the data drift alarm because ground truth arrives too slowly to be helpful
Retrain on every data drift alarm because the cost of a bad forecast is always greater than the cost of a training run

stem: A team's endpoint accepts JSON requests containing a nested `customer` object and a list of `events`. After data capture is enabled and a Data Quality monitoring schedule runs, the baseline and reports are empty or full of unexpected feature names that do not match the training columns. What should the ML engineer do?

choices.text: Set the data capture sampling percentage to 100 so that every nested field in each request is written to the capture files
Increase the instance size of the monitoring processing job so that it can parse the nested JSON records that are in the captured data
Convert the endpoint's container to accept only CSV requests so that the captured data can never contain nested fields
Provide a record preprocessor script to the monitoring schedule that flattens each captured JSON record into the training feature columns

stem: A company runs 40 models in production across several SageMaker endpoints, each with monitoring schedules for data quality, bias drift and model quality. Governance wants one view that shows which models have monitoring violations, which are missing monitoring or have inactive schedules, and which endpoints are running. What should the ML engineer use?

choices.text: A CloudWatch dashboard that the team builds by hand, with one widget for every model, schedule and violation report
An AWS Config aggregator that lists the SageMaker endpoints and reports which ones are non-compliant with monitoring rules
The Amazon SageMaker Model Dashboard, which consolidates model, endpoint and monitoring status and violations in one place
The AWS Cost Explorer SageMaker view, filtered by the cost allocation tags that the team assigned to each production model

stem: A manufacturer has five years of labeled sensor readings (about 40 numeric features per row) and wants to predict pump failures. Predictions run on millions of rows per hour and must cost very little per prediction and return in milliseconds. A stakeholder suggests sending each row to a large language model on Amazon Bedrock. What should the ML engineer recommend?

choices.text: Fine-tune a Bedrock text model on the five years of rows serialized as prompt and completion pairs so it learns the failure labels
Train a gradient-boosted tree model such as XGBoost on the labeled tabular data with SageMaker AI and serve it from an endpoint or batch job
Send each row to a Bedrock text model with a few-shot prompt that lists example rows and their failure labels before the new row
Store the historical rows in a Bedrock knowledge base and have a model retrieve similar past rows before it predicts a failure label

stem: An ML team wants to fine-tune an open-weight text model with its own training script and then host it in its own account on a GPU instance type it chooses, with control over the inference container and auto scaling settings. Which service fits these requirements?

choices.text: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, attaching the open-weight model as the generator so that it can be served without infrastructure
Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, deploying the open-weight model to a SageMaker AI endpoint on an instance type that the team selects
Amazon Bedrock, invoking the open-weight model on demand through the Converse API and paying only per input and output token
Amazon Bedrock Provisioned Throughput, buying model units for the base model so that capacity is reserved for the team's traffic

stem: A legal team wants to send scanned contract pages (images) together with typed questions to a model and get answers in one request. Some contracts are several hundred pages long and must be analyzed in a single pass. Which criteria should drive the choice of foundation model on Amazon Bedrock?

choices.text: Pick the cheapest text-only model per input token and send each page as extracted text in a separate request to keep the cost lowest
Pick a model whose supported input modalities include images and text and whose context window fits the full contract and the question
Pick an embedding model with the largest vector dimension, since it can encode the entire contract and the question into one vector
Pick the model with the highest parameter count in the catalog, since larger models always accept every input type and any document size

stem: A company is building an internal assistant on Amazon Bedrock. Answers must come from about 20,000 HR policy documents that are updated every week and must cite the source document. Answers must also follow a fixed three-part layout and a formal tone. Which TWO approaches meet these requirements with the least effort? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Fine-tune a model on question and answer pairs generated from the policies so it answers policy questions without any retrieval
Use retrieval-augmented generation with a Bedrock knowledge base over the policy documents so answers use current text and return citations
Raise the temperature and the maximum output tokens so the model writes longer, more complete answers that cover each policy
Run a continued pre-training job every week on the updated policy documents so the model learns the latest wording of every policy
Use prompt engineering with a system prompt and a few examples that show the three-part layout and the required formal tone

stem: A specialty chemicals company finds that a Bedrock model misreads its internal product codes and process jargon. The company has several gigabytes of unlabeled internal technical reports but almost no labeled question and answer pairs. It wants the model itself to understand this vocabulary. Which customization approach fits best?

choices.text: Continued pre-training on Amazon Bedrock, supplying the unlabeled technical reports so the model adapts to the company's domain language
Prompt caching on Amazon Bedrock, storing the technical reports as a cached prompt prefix so that every request includes the full vocabulary
Fine-tuning, supplying the technical reports as prompt and completion pairs so the model learns each product code as a labeled answer
Model distillation, using a larger teacher model to label the reports so that a smaller student model learns the company vocabulary

stem: A support chatbot uses a large, high-quality model on Amazon Bedrock. Its answers are good, but cost and latency are now too high at production volume. Prompts are short and varied, and Bedrock model invocation logging has stored months of production prompts. The team wants a smaller, faster model that keeps most of the large model's quality for this use case. What should the ML engineer do?

choices.text: Create a Bedrock model distillation job with the large model as teacher, a smaller model as student, and the logged prompts as input
Enable prompt caching on the large model so that repeated prompt prefixes are reused across requests and the generation step runs faster
Fine-tune the smaller model on a new dataset of answers written by the support agents, labeling thousands of prompts by hand first
Buy Provisioned Throughput model units for the large model so that every request gets reserved capacity and the per-request cost drops

stem: A company wants to route incoming support emails into eight intent categories within two weeks. It has no labeled emails today, the volume is a few thousand emails per day, and the category list may change next quarter. Which modeling approach should the ML engineer start with?

choices.text: Train a custom text classifier with SageMaker AI built-in BlazingText after a labeling team tags enough emails for every one of the categories
Train a transformer model from scratch on the archived emails with SageMaker AI distributed training so that it fits the categories exactly
Use a foundation model on Amazon Bedrock with a prompt that lists the eight categories and gives a short description and example for each
Run continued pre-training on the company's archived email text so that the model learns the support vocabulary before classifying any email

stem: An ML engineer starts an Amazon Bedrock fine-tuning job using a CSV file in Amazon S3 with two columns, question and answer. The job fails during data validation. What should the engineer change?

choices.text: Keep the CSV file and raise the number of epochs and the batch size so that the job has more passes to parse each training record
Convert the CSV file to Apache Parquet with a Snappy codec and register it in the AWS Glue Data Catalog for the customization job to read
Split the CSV file into one small text file per question and answer pair and upload all of the text files under a single S3 prefix
Convert the data to JSON Lines, one JSON record per line in the prompt and response schema the chosen base model expects, and upload it to S3

stem: A team fine-tuned a model with an Amazon Bedrock customization job, and the job completed successfully. The application still calls InvokeModel with the base model's ID, and the responses show none of the fine-tuned behavior. What must the team do to use the custom model?

choices.text: Download the custom model weights from the job's S3 output location and load them into the application, which then runs the model locally
Give the custom model serving capacity, through an on-demand custom model deployment where supported or Provisioned Throughput, and invoke that ARN
Add the custom model's name to the request body as a model variant field while the application keeps calling the same base model ID as before
Wait for the custom model to propagate to the base model ID, because Bedrock replaces the base model for the account after each completed job

stem: An ML engineer fine-tunes an open-weight 13-billion-parameter model with a SageMaker AI training job on a single-GPU instance. Full fine-tuning in 16-bit precision fails with CUDA out-of-memory errors before the first step. The budget allows only this instance type. Which change most directly lets the job fit in GPU memory?

choices.text: Use QLoRA, loading the frozen base weights in 4-bit precision and training only small low-rank adapter matrices on top of them
Raise the per-device batch size so that each step processes more samples and the GPU memory is used more efficiently per sample
Switch the weights from 16-bit to 32-bit floating point so that the optimizer states stay numerically stable during each training step
Add data parallel training across several copies of the same instance so that each instance processes a smaller share of the batches

stem: A company plans to adapt one open-weight model to six business units, each with its own task, using LoRA on SageMaker AI instead of full fine-tuning. Which TWO statements correctly describe the benefits of LoRA in this plan? (Select TWO)

choices.text: LoRA updates every weight of the base model at a lower learning rate, so it avoids overfitting while still changing the whole model
LoRA removes the need for a validation dataset because the frozen base weights prevent the adapters from overfitting the training set
LoRA trains only small low-rank matrices while the base weights stay frozen, so training needs far less GPU memory and compute
LoRA extends the base model's context window for each business unit so that every adapter can process much longer input prompts
Each LoRA adapter is a small artifact, so six adapters can share one copy of the base model instead of storing six full models

stem: An ML engineer uses the SageMaker Python SDK to fine-tune a Meta Llama model from SageMaker JumpStart on an instruction dataset in Amazon S3. The training job fails right away with an error saying the end-user license agreement was not accepted. What should the engineer do?

choices.text: Subscribe to the model in AWS Marketplace and attach the subscription ARN to the training job's IAM execution role as a new tag
Request an increase of the account's service quota for the GPU training instance type and then start the same training job again
Copy the model weights from the JumpStart bucket to the team's own S3 bucket and point the training job at the copied artifacts
Review the model license and explicitly accept the end-user license agreement in the fine-tuning call, then start the training job

stem: An Amazon Bedrock fine-tuning job fails with an access denied error when reading its training data. The data sits in an S3 bucket encrypted with a customer managed AWS KMS key. The service role passed to the job has s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on the bucket. What is the most likely fix?

choices.text: Turn off default encryption on the bucket and copy the training data again so that the job can read the objects without any KMS permission check
Allow the job's service role to use the KMS key, for example kms:Decrypt, in the key policy or in the role's policy where the key policy permits it
Create an S3 gateway VPC endpoint in the account's default VPC so that the customization job can reach the training bucket over a private network
Attach the S3 read permissions to the IAM role of the engineer who starts the job, because Bedrock reads training data with the caller's credentials

stem: A team wants to fine-tune an open-weight Llama model with its own training script, including a custom loss function. After training, the team wants to call the model through a serverless Amazon Bedrock API instead of managing endpoints. Which approach meets both requirements?

choices.text: Upload the training script to an Amazon Bedrock fine-tuning job as a custom entry point and invoke the resulting custom model on demand
Train with a SageMaker AI training job using the script, then bring the weights into Bedrock with Custom Model Import and invoke them there
Deploy the model from SageMaker JumpStart to a real-time endpoint and register that endpoint as a Bedrock base model for the Converse API
Fine-tune the model in Amazon Bedrock, export its weights to S3, and then deploy them to SageMaker AI Serverless Inference with a GPU

stem: A pharmacy chain is comparing two foundation models for answering medication questions. Its licensed pharmacists must rate each response for clinical correctness on a 1-5 scale and choose the better response in side-by-side pairs. Which Amazon Bedrock evaluation option fits?

choices.text: An automatic model evaluation job that uses the built-in prompt datasets and reports the built-in accuracy and toxicity metrics
A model evaluation job that uses an LLM as a judge with built-in metrics for correctness and completeness instead of reviewers
A human-based model evaluation job with the company's own work team of pharmacists, custom metrics, and the company prompts
A SageMaker Clarify pre-training bias report on the prompt dataset that compares label distributions across patient groups

stem: A team runs an Amazon Bedrock retrieve-and-generate evaluation on its knowledge base. Context relevance scores are high, but faithfulness scores are low: answers often contain details that do not appear in the retrieved passages. Where is the problem, and what should the team adjust first?

choices.text: In the data source: sync the knowledge base again because the vector index is likely missing the most recently uploaded documents
In the retrieval step: change the chunking strategy and embeddings model so that the knowledge base returns more relevant passages
In the evaluation itself: switch to a larger evaluator model, because a low faithfulness score means the judge cannot read the passages
In the generation step: tell the model to answer only from the provided passages and add contextual grounding checks to block the rest

stem: A team evaluates a text summarization model against reference summaries written by analysts. It wants one metric that measures word and n-gram overlap with the reference, and one that still rewards a summary that uses different words with the same meaning. Which TWO metrics should the team use? (Select TWO)

choices.text: ROUGE, which counts overlapping words and n-grams between the generated summary and the reference summary
Perplexity, which measures how likely a language model finds a text, without comparing it to any reference text
Root mean squared error, which measures the average squared distance between predicted values and true values
AUC-ROC, which measures how well a classifier ranks positive examples above negative ones across all thresholds
BERTScore, which compares contextual embeddings of the tokens in both texts to score their semantic similarity

stem: A team hosts an open-weight text model from SageMaker JumpStart on a SageMaker AI endpoint. Before each release, a SageMaker pipeline step must evaluate the model for prompt stereotyping, toxicity, and semantic robustness using built-in datasets and algorithms. Which capability fits?

choices.text: SageMaker Model Monitor bias drift monitoring, which compares live endpoint predictions with a bias baseline on a recurring schedule
SageMaker Clarify pre-training bias metrics, which measure class imbalance and label proportions across facets in the training dataset
Amazon Bedrock Guardrails content filters, which score each response for toxicity and block it before it reaches end users in production
SageMaker Clarify foundation model evaluations, run through the open-source fmeval library against the endpoint inside the pipeline

stem: An agent built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore handles warranty claims by calling tools to check orders, verify warranties, and issue replacements. Before changing the system prompt, the team wants a regression test that would catch the agent issuing a replacement without first verifying the warranty, even when the final message to the customer looks fine. What should the evaluation include?

choices.text: Ask a few customers to rate the final replies with a thumbs up or down after the prompt change, then roll back if ratings fall
Run a fixed set of test cases and compare each run's traced tool calls and arguments with the expected tool sequence for that case
Lower the temperature to zero during testing so that the agent's tool calls become deterministic and need no separate evaluation
Score only the final message against a reference reply with ROUGE, since a wrong tool sequence always lowers the overlap with that reply

stem: A team scores its Amazon Bedrock models with Bedrock model evaluation jobs that use an LLM as a judge. It now wants the same kind of judging applied to a fine-tuned model hosted outside Bedrock, using the team's own prompts. Which TWO statements describe how to set this up? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Provide the prompts as a CSV file with one column per metric so that the judge model writes a score into each column for each row
Each score from the judge model must be approved by a human work team before the evaluation job can complete and publish its report
Generate the external model's responses yourself and supply them in the prompt dataset in S3, using the bring-your-own-responses option
The judge must be the same model that is being evaluated, because a model can only grade responses written in its own style consistently
Select a supported evaluator model and choose metrics such as correctness, completeness, and helpfulness for the judge to score

stem: A retailer keeps its product catalog, prices and stock levels in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL cluster. The ML team will add embeddings of product descriptions for a shopping assistant. Each search must return only in-stock items in the shopper's price range, and the embeddings must change in the same transaction that updates a product row. Which vector store fits best?

choices.text: The pgvector extension in the existing Aurora PostgreSQL cluster, storing a vector column in the product table and filtering with SQL
An Amazon OpenSearch Serverless vector search collection, with a Lambda function that copies each product row into the index after commit
A Bedrock knowledge base with an S3 data source holding one exported file per product, re-synced each hour to pick up stock changes
An Amazon S3 Vectors index in a vector bucket, with price and stock copied into each vector's filterable metadata by a nightly export job

stem: An ML engineer creates an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base that uses Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2 with 1,024 output dimensions. The vector index in the Amazon OpenSearch Serverless collection was created from an older template whose knn_vector field has dimension 1536. Every ingestion job fails for all documents. What should the engineer do?

choices.text: Turn on the normalize option for Titan Text Embeddings V2 so that each 1,024-value vector is padded with zeros to the 1536 values the index expects
Create a new vector index whose knn_vector field uses dimension 1024, update the knowledge base to use it, and run the ingestion job again
Change the vector field's engine from faiss to lucene, because only the lucene engine accepts vectors shorter than the dimension in the mapping
Raise the maximum indexing capacity of the OpenSearch Serverless account so that the collection can accept the larger 1536-value vectors

stem: A team stores support-article embeddings in an Amazon S3 Vectors index with PutVectors. To return the article text with each result, they attach the full text as a metadata key. PutVectors now fails with a metadata size error for long articles, although the text is never used in query filters. Which change fixes this?

choices.text: Move the article text into a separately named metadata key in the same index, because the filterable size limit applies to each key rather than to the vector
Switch the index distance metric from cosine to euclidean, because euclidean indexes store vectors more compactly and leave more room for metadata on each vector
Create a new vector index that declares the text key as non-filterable metadata, which has a larger size allowance, and write the vectors to that index
Store the vectors as 16-bit floats instead of 32-bit floats, so that the space saved on every vector can be used for the larger text metadata value

stem: A company's Bedrock knowledge base must answer questions about resolved support tickets within about a minute of the ticket closing. Tickets close a few hundred times an hour. Today a workflow writes each ticket to the S3 data source and an ingestion job runs nightly. Which approach meets the freshness goal with the least operational overhead?

choices.text: Add a custom data source and call the IngestKnowledgeBaseDocuments API from the ticket workflow, so that each closed ticket is chunked and embedded directly
Schedule StartIngestionJob every minute with Amazon EventBridge Scheduler, so that each run picks up the tickets written to Amazon S3 since the last run
Write each ticket into the OpenSearch Serverless vector index with the bulk API, using the same field names the knowledge base mapped for text and vectors
Turn on S3 Event Notifications for the data source bucket, because the knowledge base subscribes to them and re-syncs changed objects automatically

stem: A media company wants a RAG assistant over 5,000 hours of recorded podcast episodes stored as MP3 files in Amazon S3. Each answer must cite the episode and the time in the episode where the supporting passage starts so listeners can jump to it. Which ingestion design meets this requirement?

choices.text: Transcribe each episode with Amazon Transcribe and ingest each full transcript as one chunk, citing the episode start time with every answer given
Add the MP3 files directly to the knowledge base's S3 data source with the default parser, which transcribes audio and keeps the time of every chunk
Embed fixed-length audio clips with Amazon Titan Multimodal Embeddings G1, storing the clip start time as metadata next to each audio vector
Transcribe each episode with Amazon Transcribe, split the timed transcript into passages, and store each passage with episode and start time metadata

stem: An ML engineer is setting up an existing Amazon OpenSearch Serverless vector search collection as the vector store for a new Amazon Bedrock knowledge base. Which TWO steps are required before the first ingestion job can succeed? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Enable fine-grained access control in OpenSearch Dashboards on the collection and map the knowledge base service role to the all_access role
Add the knowledge base service role to the collection's data access policy with permissions to read and write the index and documents
Set the shard and replica counts on the vector index to match the number of documents expected in the data source after the first sync
Recreate the collection as a time series collection so that each ingestion job appends new vectors with a timestamp it can roll back to
Create a vector index with a knn_vector field whose dimension matches the embedding model, plus fields for chunk text and metadata

stem: A team stores 3 million document embeddings in Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with pgvector. They built an HNSW index for Euclidean (L2) distance. Queries rank results by cosine distance (the <=> operator) with LIMIT 10, and EXPLAIN shows a sequential scan, making each search take seconds. What should the ML engineer do?

choices.text: Rebuild the HNSW index with the cosine distance operator class so that the distance the index was built for matches the queries
Replace the HNSW index with an IVFFlat index built for L2 distance, because only IVFFlat indexes can serve cosine distance ordering in queries
Raise the hnsw.ef_search setting for the session so that the planner treats the existing index as precise enough to use for cosine queries
Run VACUUM ANALYZE on the table so that the planner updates its statistics and begins choosing the HNSW index for the cosine distance queries

stem: A Bedrock knowledge base already indexes product manuals from an S3 data source. The engineering team also wants pages from the company's Confluence Cloud space, which requires sign-in, included in the same assistant's answers. Which approach requires the least custom code and ongoing maintenance?

choices.text: Write a Lambda function that exports Confluence pages to the S3 data source each night and then starts an ingestion job for that bucket
Point a web crawler data source at the Confluence space URLs so that the knowledge base follows links and indexes each page it can reach
Create a second knowledge base for Confluence and change the application to query both knowledge bases and merge the two sets of results
Add a Confluence data source to the existing knowledge base with credentials stored in AWS Secrets Manager, and sync it on its own schedule

stem: A bank loads 12,000 FAQ files into a Bedrock knowledge base. Each file holds exactly one short question and its answer of about 120 words. With fixed-size chunking at 60 tokens, retrieved chunks often contain only the question or only the answer. Which chunking setting fits this content best?

choices.text: Use semantic chunking with a low breakpoint percentile threshold so that every sentence boundary inside a file starts a new and separate chunk
Use hierarchical chunking with 60-token child chunks so that the child chunks hold the questions and parent chunks hold only the answers
Use no chunking, so that each FAQ file becomes exactly one chunk that always keeps the question together with its complete answer text
Keep fixed-size chunking at 60 tokens and raise the overlap percentage so that each chunk repeats a large part of the previous chunk's text

stem: A manufacturer indexes 200 router manuals that share most of their wording. A chunk such as "Hold the reset button for 10 seconds" contains no model name, so questions about model R7 often retrieve steps from model R5. The chunk size is reasonable. Which change fixes this best at ingestion time?

choices.text: Add a custom transformation Lambda function that prepends the model name and section title to each chunk and stores the model as metadata
Switch to semantic chunking so that the chunk boundaries follow topic changes in each manual rather than a fixed number of tokens per chunk
Reduce the embedding dimension from 1,024 to 256 so that small differences in wording between manuals carry more weight in similarity search
Increase the number of retrieved results from 5 to 25 so that a chunk from the correct manual is very likely to appear among the results returned

stem: A team builds its own retrieval pipeline with Cohere Embed on Amazon Bedrock. A batch job embedded all 2 million documents, reusing the query code, so every call used input_type "search_query". Queries also use "search_query". Retrieval quality is noticeably worse than in the vendor's benchmarks. What should the team change?

choices.text: Keep the stored embeddings and switch the queries to Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2, so that queries and documents use two separate models
Keep the embeddings and normalize every stored vector to unit length, because the input_type only affects the scale of the vectors returned
Re-embed the documents with input_type "search_document" and keep "search_query" for the user queries, so each side uses the type the model expects
Re-embed both the documents and the queries with input_type "classification", because that type yields the most general purpose vectors

stem: An online store wants shoppers to search 4 million product photos either by typing text such as "red leather ankle boots" or by uploading a photo of a similar item. Product photos have no reliable captions. Which embedding approach supports both kinds of search with one vector index?

choices.text: Embed the photos and the text queries with Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2, sending each photo as a base64 string in the request's text input field
Embed the photos, typed queries and uploaded query photos with Amazon Titan Multimodal Embeddings G1, which maps images and text into one space
Run Amazon Rekognition DetectLabels on each photo, store the label names as keywords, and match the typed queries with a keyword search only
Generate a caption for every catalog photo with a text model, embed only the captions with Titan Text Embeddings V2, and embed queries as text

stem: Documents in a Bedrock knowledge base each have a .metadata.json file with "publish_date": "2026-03-15" stored as a string. A retrieval filter using greaterThan on publish_date to keep only documents newer than 2025 returns errors or no results. What should the ML engineer change?

choices.text: Move the publish date into the first line of each document's text so that semantic search ranks the newer documents above the older ones
Change the retrieval filter from greaterThan to stringContains with the value "2026" so that it compares dates stored as strings correctly
Rename the attribute to x-amz-bedrock-kb-date so that the knowledge base recognizes it as a built-in date field with range comparisons
Store the date as a number such as 20260315 in the metadata files, re-sync the data source, and filter with greaterThan on that numeric value

stem: An insurer is building its own RAG pipeline into Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector. Source documents are scanned, multi-page claim forms saved as image-only PDFs with tables of line items. The extracted text must keep table rows intact before chunking and embedding. Which preprocessing step fits?

choices.text: Run Amazon Comprehend DetectEntities on each PDF file so that every table row is returned as one entity that can be embedded on its own later
Send the PDF bytes directly to Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2, which reads the scanned page images and keeps every table row inside one vector
Run Amazon Rekognition DetectText on each page image and join the detected lines from top to bottom into plain text that is then chunked by size
Run asynchronous Amazon Textract document analysis with the TABLES and LAYOUT features, and convert each table to row-wise text before chunking

stem: A team embeds 1,500-token chunks with an embedding model whose maximum input is much shorter than that, with truncation set to "END" so that requests do not fail. No errors are reported, but questions answered by text near the end of a chunk are rarely retrieved. What is the most effective fix?

choices.text: Reduce the chunk size so that every chunk fits within the embedding model's input limit, then re-chunk and re-embed the corpus
Normalize all stored vectors to unit length so that long chunks no longer dominate the similarity scores computed against queries
Raise the number of results returned per query from 5 to 20 so that chunks whose ending text was cut off still make it into the results
Increase the chunk overlap to 50 percent so that the text at the end of each chunk also appears at the start of the following chunk

stem: A team runs a custom RAG pipeline that stores 40 million chunk embeddings in Amazon OpenSearch Service. Which TWO changes require the team to re-chunk or re-embed the entire stored corpus before the change takes effect? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Changing the number of chunks retrieved per query from 5 to 8 and adjusting the minimum similarity score threshold
Switching the text generation model that writes the final answer to a newer model with a larger context window size
Changing the chunk size and overlap that the pipeline uses to split every document before the chunks are embedded
Adding a reranking model that reorders the top 50 retrieved chunks before the best ones are sent to the generator
Replacing the embedding model with a different model, or changing the output dimension setting of the current model

stem: Before fine-tuning a model on Amazon Bedrock, a company must find which of its 300 S3 buckets contain personal data, then create copies of 2 million English chat transcripts in which names, phone numbers and addresses are replaced by their entity type. Which TWO services should the ML engineer use? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Amazon CloudWatch Logs data protection policies on the transcript buckets to mask personal data in objects as they are written to S3
Amazon Macie sensitive data discovery to find and report which buckets and objects across the account contain personal data
Amazon Inspector scans of the S3 buckets to find objects with personal data and to replace each match with a masked placeholder value
AWS Glue Data Quality rulesets on the transcript tables to detect and rewrite each name, phone number and address in the text field
Amazon Comprehend asynchronous PII detection jobs in redaction mode to write copies of the transcripts with each PII entity replaced

stem: An AWS Glue job prepares a JSONL fine-tuning dataset of prompt and completion pairs. Recent runs included empty completions, very short completions and many repeated prompts. The ML engineer wants each run to measure these problems and keep failing records out of the training output automatically. What should the engineer add?

choices.text: An Amazon Bedrock model evaluation job that scores the dataset records for completeness before the fine-tuning job is started
An AWS Glue Data Quality ruleset in the job, using row-level results to send records that fail the rules to a quarantine prefix
Amazon CloudWatch anomaly detection on the size of each output file so that unusual datasets stop the fine-tuning job from running
An Amazon Macie job with custom data identifiers that flags empty or very short completion values as sensitive findings for review

stem: A company fine-tuned a model for customer support on 400,000 past chats. About 90 percent came from customers in North America; chats from India and Nigeria, now growing markets, are rare. Answers to customers in those markets are noticeably worse. Which TWO data steps address the cause? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Increase the number of training epochs on the same dataset so that the model has more passes to learn the rare regional examples
Add a guardrail denied topic for regional dialects so that the model declines to answer questions phrased in an unfamiliar style
Remove the customer region field from every training record so that the model cannot learn any difference between the regions
Collect or create additional high-quality chats for the underrepresented regions and rebalance the dataset before fine-tuning again
Measure how the training records are distributed across customer region and language variety, and compare it with current traffic

stem: A team augmented 20,000 support examples with paraphrases, giving 100,000 records, then randomly split them 90/10 into training and evaluation sets for fine-tuning. The fine-tuned model scores very high on the evaluation set but performs much worse in production. Which data fix addresses the most likely cause?

choices.text: Shuffle the 100,000 records again with a different random seed and repeat the 90/10 split, then fine-tune and evaluate the model again
Raise the evaluation share from 10 to 30 percent with the same random split so that the evaluation score has a smaller margin of error
Split by original example so each one and all its paraphrases land in the same set, and remove near-duplicates across the two sets
Remove all paraphrased records from the evaluation set only, so that it holds only original examples while training keeps the paraphrases

stem: An insurer runs a claims-summary feature on an Amazon Bedrock model through the Converse API. Auditors require every prompt and model response to be kept for one year, and engineers want to search the last two weeks of requests interactively while debugging. Nothing is recorded today. What should the ML engineer do?

choices.text: Enable Bedrock model invocation logging in the Region with both an S3 bucket and a CloudWatch Logs log group as destinations, and set retention on each destination
Create a high-resolution CloudWatch dashboard on the AWS/Bedrock namespace so that every invocation, with its prompt and response, can be searched for one year
Turn on AWS CloudTrail data events for the Bedrock runtime API and query the trail with Athena, because each event stores the full prompt and the model's response text
Enable data capture on the model, the same way as on a SageMaker endpoint, so that the request and response payloads are written to an S3 prefix for the audit team

stem: A retail chatbot calls an Amazon Bedrock model on demand. Every weekday between 12:00 and 13:00, some users get errors. CloudWatch shows that `InvocationThrottles` for the model ID rises sharply in that hour, while `InvocationServerErrors` stays at zero and `InvocationLatency` is normal. What should the ML engineer do FIRST?

choices.text: Open a support case about a service fault, because server-side errors in the Bedrock runtime cause intermittent failures that only appear at certain hours
Add retries with exponential backoff and jitter, and route the calls through a cross-Region inference profile or request a higher quota for the peak hour
Switch the chatbot to a larger model in the same family, because a model with more parameters is allocated a higher request quota for on-demand use in each Region
Increase the `maxTokens` inference parameter so that each answer completes in one call and the client sends fewer follow-up requests during the busy lunch hour

stem: A support agent built with an open-source framework runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime and calls four tools. Some answers come back incomplete, and the team suspects that tool calls fail silently. They need step-level visibility into each request. Which TWO actions should the ML engineer take? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Open the CloudWatch generative AI observability view, filter traces by session, and inspect tool spans that have an error status or unusually long duration
Enable SageMaker Model Monitor model quality monitoring for the agent so that each failed tool call is reported as a constraint violation in the next monitoring run
Raise the agent's model temperature so that the model retries a failed tool with different arguments instead of returning the partial result to the user
Turn on CloudTrail data events for the agent's Region so that the reasoning steps and tool inputs of each conversation turn are stored in the trail for later review
Enable CloudWatch Transaction Search and instrument the agent with AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry so AgentCore Observability records a trace with a span for each model and tool call

stem: A web chat streams answers from an Amazon Bedrock model with the ConverseStream API. Users say some answers stop in the middle of a sentence, but every stream finishes without an error and `InvocationClientErrors` is zero. The ML engineer needs a production metric that shows how often answers are cut off. What should the engineer do?

choices.text: Create an alarm on the `InvocationClientErrors` metric for the model ID, because every truncated answer is counted there as a rejected request from the chat client
Alarm on the average `OutputTokenCount` metric for the model ID, because a falling average shows exactly which responses were cut off before they were finished
Enable the contextual grounding check in a guardrail, because it flags responses that end early and reports them as interventions in the guardrail metrics
Read the stop reason in the stream's final message event and publish a custom CloudWatch metric each time it is `max_tokens`, then alarm on that rate

stem: A travel company runs a supervisor agent and three specialist agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime. A few requests a day pass work back and forth between two specialists until the request times out, and token spend for those sessions is very high. Today each agent's logs are viewed separately. How should the ML engineer detect these coordination failures?

choices.text: Alarm on the average `InvocationLatency` of the model ID that the agents share, because a handoff loop shows up as a slower average latency across all model calls
Raise the session timeout of the supervisor agent so that looping requests have time to finish, and compare the final answers with those of normal requests
Propagate one session ID and trace context through every agent so each request is one trace, and alarm on a custom metric of handoffs or tokens per session
Add a denied topic to the agents' guardrail that describes repeated delegation, so that a loop between two specialists is blocked and counted as an intervention

stem: A bank's FAQ assistant on Amazon Bedrock was approved after an offline evaluation. Since then, the document set and user questions have changed, and the team worries that answer quality is drifting. Model invocation logs are already delivered to Amazon S3. The team wants a weekly, automated quality signal without human labeling. What should the ML engineer build?

choices.text: A SageMaker Model Monitor data quality schedule that compares this week's prompts with the training baseline of the foundation model and reports drifted features
A weekly job that samples logged prompts and responses, runs a Bedrock LLM-as-a-judge evaluation job on them, and publishes the scores as CloudWatch metrics
A CloudWatch alarm on the weekly sum of `OutputTokenCount` for the model, because answers that become shorter or longer indicate that answer quality has dropped
A guardrail word filter containing the phrases that bad answers usually contain, with a weekly report of the number of words that the filter blocked in responses

stem: An internal assistant uses an Amazon Bedrock model. The CloudWatch dashboard shows the Average statistic of `InvocationLatency` at about 1.8 seconds, which meets the 3-second target, yet many users report waits of 8 seconds or more. How should the ML engineer change the monitoring?

choices.text: Graph and alarm on the p90 and p99 percentile statistics of `InvocationLatency`, so the slow tail that users notice is measured against the target
Enable model invocation logging and remove the latency widget, because the logged response text also gives the wait time that each user experienced
Replace the latency metric with the `Invocations` metric, because the number of calls per minute shows directly how long each user had to wait
Switch the dashboard to the Sum statistic of `InvocationLatency`, because the total latency per minute shows how long the slowest users waited for answers

stem: Each quarter, a compliance team classifies about 5 million archived customer emails with an Amazon Bedrock model. Today a fleet of Lambda functions calls InvokeModel on demand for each email; the run hits throttling and costs more than planned. Results are needed within a few days. Which approach reduces cost MOST?

choices.text: Raise the reserved concurrency of the Lambda functions so the run finishes in fewer hours, because Bedrock bills on-demand inference by the hour of model use
Route the Lambda calls through a cross-Region inference profile, because spreading the requests across Regions lowers the price charged for each input and output token
Buy Provisioned Throughput with no commitment for the week of the run, because reserved model units are always billed at a lower rate per token than on-demand calls
Write the emails as JSONL records to Amazon S3 and run a Bedrock batch inference job, which is priced lower than on-demand and writes the results back to S3

stem: An ML engineer is deciding where Amazon Bedrock prompt caching will lower cost and latency. Which workload benefits MOST from enabling it?

choices.text: A sentiment classifier for short social media posts, where each request contains only a 30-word instruction followed by the text of one post
A monthly report generator that sends a long finance glossary once on the first business day and otherwise makes no calls during the month
An agent that sends the same long system prompt and tool definitions on every turn, with users making several turns within a few minutes
A nightly job that summarizes 20,000 different contracts, where each request contains one contract and a short instruction of about 40 words

stem: A team is comparing on-demand inference and Provisioned Throughput for a new Amazon Bedrock workload and asks the ML engineer to confirm how each is billed. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Provisioned Throughput is free for the first model unit, and only additional model units beyond the first one are charged per hour of usage
Provisioned Throughput bills per token like on-demand, but at a lower rate per token, and it scales its model units to zero automatically at night
On-demand inference requires a one-month or six-month commitment, which in return guarantees that requests are never throttled in busy hours
On-demand inference is billed for the input and output tokens that each request processes, with no capacity commitment and no charge while idle
Provisioned Throughput is billed for each model unit per hour for the whole term, whether or not the workload sends any requests during that time
